_comment: Reviewed explanations of each divergence the generator finds between docs/product/data-dictionary.md and the live schema. Keys are table|field|kind exactly as the generator computes them. With --strict, the generator fails on a divergence that is not informational and has no entry here, on an entry whose divergence no longer exists, and on a policy note whose list differs from the table's live policies in either direction (a policy it names that does not exist, or a live policy it does not name). Status: 'explained' (an ADR records it), 'stricter than the dictionary' (the schema enforces more), 'not built (milestone N)', or 'founder ruling needed'.

source_document|kind|enumeration differs.text: era_export is an eighth document kind: a practice-management system's ERA export (CO-03), loaded by the parse job into the same remittance, claim and line rows an 835 makes. It requires source_document.format_id, one of the vendor format registry's four ERA formats (source_document_format_of_era_export). x12_835 stays the CHECK's first value. data-dictionary.md stays verbatim and this document records the divergence.

rule_record|record_type|enumeration diff.by: ADR 0008 (decision and revisit condition); ADR 0064 (the founder's answer of 2026-10-21 to PR 6b's Q3 (a))
rule_record|record_type|enumeration diff.text: denial_category is a sixteenth record type because the rules reference keeps the denial classification 'as a rule record'. ADR 0008 says this departs from the dictionary's fifteen and is raised with the founder; its revisit condition waits on that ruling. Approving this document approves the sixteenth type; data-dictionary.md stays verbatim and this document records the divergence (reconciliation-001, D2). locality_map_plus_four is a seventeenth (migration 20261105090000): the ZIP+4 file's localities of a ZIP that spans more than one, one record per such ZIP keyed by its five digits, which the founder's answer of 2026-10-21 to PR 6b's Q3 (a) admits as a granted exception to reconciliation-001's rule-table check (ADR 0064; tools/engine-freeze/exception.json names the one statement); approving this document approves it too, and the dictionary stays verbatim.

priced_line|expected_unrounded|retyped.text: numeric with no scale keeps the exact unrounded value; numeric(18,6) would round it (ADR 0029: golden line G09 carries more than six decimal places). CLAUDE.md rule 2 keeps the unrounded value beside the rounded one.

line_status|reason|encryption.text: A person's free text can name a patient, so it is encrypted with the practice data key; ENCRYPTED_COLUMNS in packages/db/src/crypto/cipher.ts lists it and the catalog test requires its enc:v1 CHECK.

case_line|written_off_text|encryption.text: The write-off's free text, beside the closed written_off_reason code the dictionary lists.

case_line|reopen_reason|encryption.text: The reopen reason is a person's free text.

packet_version|narrative|encryption.text: The narrative is the person's words, encrypted with the practice key; identifiers stay placeholders until export.

submission|reference|encryption.text: The payer's reference (a portal confirmation, a fax receipt) is free text a person types.

payer_response|notes|encryption.text: Notes on a payer response are a person's free text.

ledger_entry|reason|encryption.text: A ledger correction's reason is the person's words, encrypted; the amount, stage and evidence stay plain.

model_call|actor|renamed.text: The dictionary's single actor field is two columns: actor_kind (user, service or evaluation) and actor_id (null only for a synthetic evaluation call), with CHECKs model_call_actor and model_call_evaluation_is_synthetic.

model_call|updated_at|convention.text: A model call is written once (model_call_rules: 'a model call never changes; only the reviewer's decision is recorded, once'); reviewed_at records that one later change.

eval_example|updated_at|convention.text: An evaluation example is never changed or deleted (eval_example_rules).

audit_event|updated_at|convention.text: audit_event is append-only (audit_event_append_only, audit_event_no_truncate). The dictionary's own row gives `at` as its time, which the schema has.

usage_snapshot|updated_at|convention.text: A usage snapshot never changes (usage_snapshot_kept: 'a usage snapshot never changes').

job||missing table.by: ADR 0004; ADR 0049; README (pg-boss connects as its own login in the role tp_queue, which owns the pgboss schema)
job||missing table.text: The queue is pg-boss's own tables, which pg-boss installs in its own schema pgboss on start, owned by tp_queue, outside schema public and outside this document. The product's record of each job is job_run (singleton key, practice_id, idempotency key, attempts, outcome).

job_run||classification.text: The dictionary files job_run under 'Operations (no PHI by design)', and it holds no PHI column. Because it carries practice_id NOT NULL, the catalog rule requires a registry row, FORCE RLS and the tenant policy, so a practice's job history is tenant-scoped like its data.

notification||classification.by: ADR 0039 (Counts and totals only, in the schema)
notification||classification.text: The dictionary lists notification with user_id only. The schema adds practice_id NOT NULL and subject_id, so it is registered and tenant-scoped; its figures columns admit only integer counts and integer-cent totals (figures_are_counts, figures_are_cents), so no PHI can be written to it.

digest||classification.by: ADR 0039 (Counts and totals only, in the schema)
digest||classification.text: digest has practice_id in the dictionary too; with practice_id NOT NULL the catalog rule registers it. Counts and totals only.

legal_hold||missing table.text: Lifecycle tables for export and deletion are milestone 12 work, not started; /p/[practiceId]/settings/data shows placeholders. Kept in milestone 12 by CO-08.

export_job||missing table.text: As legal_hold. Not to be confused with the job type 'export' in job_run.

claim|index (practice_id, payer_claim_co.text: payer_claim_control_number is encrypted, so the index is claim_by_payer_claim_control_number on (practice_id, payer_claim_control_number_hash), the deterministic hash the dictionary's own note asks for.

policies.text: Members read their own organizations. Platform administrators also read every one, create group and firm organizations and edit them (the console). The billing role tp_billing reads every row and sets billing_customer_ref only while it is null.

'By grant or ownership' is implemented as the registered tenant policy on app.practice_ids, which the handler sets from the person's memberships intersected with grants in force (effective_practice_access). Platform administrators create practices; only the practice's administrators update it (restrictive).
Self and administrators, as the dictionary says; administrators may only create an invited user without MFA.
Adds a person's read of their own memberships and platform administrators. An organization administrator may not add a person already known to another organization (user_known_elsewhere).
Practice administrators approve and revoke; the practice's administrators and the grantee read. No route or screen yet approves or revokes a grant (CO-08).

Parties to it read it, as the dictionary says; platform administrators also read and record agreements. An e-signed agreement is recorded only through record_esigned_agreement(), executable by tp_esign alone (migration 20261101100000).

Platform administrators create one; members of the practice's own group and platform administrators read it; the application never updates one. ADR 0028 extends support grants to contract specialists and ADR 0038 to reimbursement reviewers (read-only); PRD 3 names support engineers only.

plan.subject: Remittance duplicate key
plan.where: PRD 8 (PRD.md:318); PRD 10 step 8 (PRD.md:428); CLAUDE.md Conventions; Data dictionary
plan.says: PRD 8: unique on (practice, sender, ISA13, TRN02). PRD 10: (practice, payee, ISA13, TRN02, BPR02), as CLAUDE.md's idempotency line said until CO-02's pull request corrected it. Data dictionary: unique (practice_id, sender_id, isa13, trn02, bpr02_cents).
plan.schema: remittance_once UNIQUE (practice_id, sender_id, isa13, trn02, bpr02_cents), the dictionary's key; ADR 0031 also treats a resend under a new ISA13 with the same payee, TRN02, TRN03, BPR02 and BPR16 as a duplicate. An ERA export (provenance era_export, ADR 0060, D12 a) is keyed by remittance_export_once (practice_id, payee_npi, trn02, bpr_credit_debit, bpr02_cents, bpr16_date) over export rows, and the 835 is authoritative between the two (D13 a).
plan.status: founder ruling needed (reconciliation-001, decision D2): confirm the dictionary's key; PRD.md and the dictionary stay verbatim as the imported plan, and CLAUDE.md's idempotency line is corrected to the key and ADR 0031's resend rule

plan.subject: CO-12 names tables that do not exist
plan.says: practice_settings gains two columns; packet_export records five parts.
plan.schema: Settings are practice.settings jsonb (the dictionary's own practice row), guarded by CHECKs and practice_setting_keys(). No packet_export table exists: an export is five columns on packet_version (export_pdf_key, export_csv_key, export_sha256, export_csv_sha256, exported_at), with the verifier's report over what it rendered (export_verifier_report) and the reimbursement reviewer's attestation over its two SHA-256 (attested_by, attested_at, attestation; 20261103090000, ADR 0061, D16), made only once the attester has downloaded both files since the export: each download is an audit_event (packet_export_pdf_downloaded, packet_export_csv_downloaded) that audit_event_packet_download records only on a connection that is not the worker's own login (app_session_is_job(), the marker role tp_job), for a person who may read the export, read by packet_export_downloads_of_actor(), so no table is added (the founder's addition of 2026-10-18).
plan.status: proposed (reconciliation-001, decisions D26 and D29): two keys in practice.settings; a new packet_export table with its parts. Built in part: the export's verifier report and the attestation on packet_version, with the downloads it needs in audit_event (20261103090000, ADR 0061, D16), are approved as the packet_version and audit_event sections describe them, and only the rest is a proposal

plan.subject: CO-12 'roles enum' and 'enum' columns
plan.says: Add financial_reviewer and auditor to the roles enum; readiness_grade and deadline_verification_status as enums.
plan.schema: There are no PostgreSQL enum types. Roles are text with CHECK membership_role_check and role_permission_role_check (10 roles); every enumeration is a CHECK. deadline_verification_status is built so (20261103090000, ADR 0061): packet_version.deadline_verification_status is text generated from the version's content, with CHECK packet_version_deadline_verification_status_check (verified, unverified, not_applicable).
plan.status: proposed (CO-12; the schema's rule that every enumeration is text with a CHECK, reconciliation-001 D2 on C3): readiness_grade and the two roles, still to come (PR 8, PR 14). Built in part: packet_version.deadline_verification_status, text generated from the content with its CHECK (20261103090000, ADR 0061; what verified means is D17 a), is approved as the packet_version section describes it, and only the rest is a proposal

plan.subject: CO-12 case_transition_log has no practice_id
plan.says: CO-12: case_id, from_state, to_state, actor_id, allowed, reason, at. CLAUDE.md: every table that can hold PHI has practice_id and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY.
plan.status: proposed (reconciliation-001, decision D25): practice_id, a registry row, FORCE RLS; reason a closed code

plan.subject: CO-12 screening tables 'outside the RLS catalog'
plan.where: Change Order 001, CO-04 and CO-12; packages/db/src/catalog.ts
plan.says: CO-04: no practice_id, outside the RLS catalog. The catalog test: a table without RLS is global and the application role may only read it.
plan.schema: Built as prospect_request is (migration 20261104090000, ADR 0062): screening_prospect, screening_upload, screening_run and screening_result, a fifth, the platform place-of-service split the engine needs (no rule record carries one), screening_place_of_service_split until migration 20261105090000 renamed it place_of_service_split, since then also every practice's default for a place it has not set, pinned on each pricing run (ADR 0064), and four more by the founder's rulings of 2026-10-20 (audit #57): screening_outcome, the counts-only outcome every screening leaves, kept with no end date; screening_lead and screening_lead_product, the frozen summary of a converted or consenting practice's screening, kept 12 months from the upload; and marketing_campaign, the campaign codes the founder lists. Each is in public with RLS forced and the owner's policy alone, no practice_id, no phi_table_registry row and no privilege for any other role. The application writes them only through submit_screening() and reject_screening_upload() (which also write the outcome), reads a result by its link token's SHA-256, records its first open through screening_result_opened(), converts it through convert_screening() (which keeps the summary with the request), withdraws a consent summary through screening_lead_withdraw(), and the console approves the split through console_approve_place_of_service_split() (console_approve_screening_split() before migration 20261105090000) and lists a campaign through console_register_marketing_campaign() (all SECURITY DEFINER); the platform jobs use operator_screening_*() as tp_operator, the release's keyed records read by the run's own keys (operator_screening_run_keys(), operator_screening_run_records(); audit #53). An upload stores its row count and coded reasons, the SHA-256 of the rows accepted (computed by submit_screening() from the rows it stores; never a hash of the file, which holds the rows left out, and none on a refused upload), and of the rows of fewer than 11 claim lines the browser left out three numbers alone, and since migration 20261105090000 three more of the Medicare rows it left out for a quarter outside the release's loaded content (the founder's answer of 2026-10-21 to PR 6b's Q6 (a)), never a byte of the file; a prospect's ZIP+4 is kept only when its ZIP's locality_map record needs it (ADR 0064); no row of fewer than 11 claim lines is stored (the CMS small-cell standard, the founder's ruling of 2026-10-18), and a practice keeps one accepted screening and one kept summary at a time (a later one of the same ZIP and practice name, or the same contact address, replaces it, a summary at the later screening's completion; a summary kept with a request passes to the later screening, carrying the request, only when its ZIP and practice name match, and is deleted with no successor when the address alone matches, its request kept without one), so no two can be subtracted into a smaller cell. An outcome holds bands, whole-percent shares, closed codes and flags, never a name, an email, a ZIP, an exact count, a date or a dollar figure, and is unlinked when its screening goes and then sealed; a summary's claim-line sums are 0 or at least 11 by CHECK. The rules: screening_outcome_rules (fixed columns, one-way stage, flags and first open once, sealed once unlinked; DELETE and TRUNCATE refused), screening_lead_rules (fixed but for its link, first open, request, withdrawal token, reminder and a withdrawal's expiry), screening_lead_kept (deleted only on expiry or withdrawal, replacement, or its request's deletion), and marketing_campaign append-only; catalog.ts is unchanged, and SEC-17 reads the catalog for PHI-shaped columns across the nine tables.
plan.status: decided (reconciliation-001, decision D18 a, approved 2026-10-17; the founder's rulings of 2026-10-20 on audit #57, decisions 7 to 12 and 17 to 19) and built; approving this document approves the fifth table and the four of audit #57, which CO-12 does not list
